claude_proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemComponentMechanics.triggered_reaction
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The item has a genuine reaction-shaped sub-ability, but magic-item mechanics only admit passive and activation components. Encoding it as an ordinary activation would drop the trigger semantics.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can take a Reaction when another creature casts a spell that targets only you"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: shared_charge_pool_across_magic_item_components
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell table, Spell Absorption, and Retributive Strike all operate on the same 50-charge pool. Current composite magic items do not provide one shared resource that multiple components can consume, gain, and read.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "This staff has 50 charges" / "gaining a number of charges equal to the absorbed spell's level" / "damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: DiceAmount.from_charge_pool
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike damage is derived from the current number of charges in the item, multiplied by a constant. Existing DiceAmount variants cover fixed dice, level scaling, spent resource, and linked damage, but not current pool state.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "you take Force damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff" / "a creature takes Force damage equal to 6 times the number of charges in the staff"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: charge_gain_from_trigger_context_with_overflow_branch
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Spell Absorption both cancels the triggering spell and gains charges equal to the triggering spell's level, then branches into an explosion if the pool would exceed 50. The surface has no way to gain charges from trigger context or branch on overflow.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "the staff absorbs the magic of the spell, canceling its effect and gaining a number of charges equal to the absorbed spell's level. However, if doing so brings the staff's total number of charges above 50, the staff explodes"
